transcript_header:
Date: 2025-05-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 78 minutes
Location: Zoom - Redwood internal enablement
Attendees: Priya Shah, Evan Li, Hannah Torres, Marta King; roleplay: Tom Rivera, Sana Iqbal
transcript_summary: Internal demo clinic with reverse roleplay (customer-as-AE) to refine messaging and competitive rebuttals. Focus on cost/latency framing, dedicated vs hosted narrative, VPC/on-prem questions, and a short live-demo failure recovery script. Action: update demo script, produce latency clip, schedule procurement roleplay.
transcript_topics: technical deep dive - latency and batch/caching
transcript:
[00:00] Priya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick agenda — reverse roleplay then feedback, we want rough and honest. Evan youre going to demo but start with the friction question.
[00:22] Evan: cool, yep. Tom youre playing the product lead, ask us like youd in a discovery, push on cost and latency.
[00:34] Tom (roleplay): ok so were a mid-sized healthcare app, latency is huge for triage flow, and finance wants to keep cloud spend predictable. why Redwood vs Anthropic or Cohere?
[00:50] Priya: great opener, Id lead with production economics — not just model quality. say: "we help keep latency predictable while lowering per-token cost using smart batching, caching, and routing". then we show a concrete chart.
[01:10] Tom: follow-up — can you guarantee low p95 at peak? our app has bursts.
[01:20] Evan: yep so we walk through Dedicated: reserved GPU pools with autoscale and burst cap, SLA-backed latency targets, and fallback policy to smaller variants. mention KV cache to reduce repeated token compute.
[01:38] Sana (roleplay): what about private deployment? we have PHI concerns and a strict vendor policy.
[01:45] Hannah: call out Redwood Private: VPC mode, on-prem option, customer-managed KMS/HSM, and audit logs. note: SOC 2 and ISO in progress or already completed — speaker mumbles dates sometimes, careful there.
[02:05] Tom: procurement will ask about egress and data residency.
[02:10] Priya: right, for procurement script: "we do not persist customer prompts in hosted unless explicitly configured; for Dedicated and Private, you control retention and keys". put that in one-pager.
[02:30] Evan: demo time — showing the triage flow with streaming responses. watch for when the LLM hallucinates an actionable recommendation — we must show our guardrails and function-calling.
[02:45] [demo starts — screen share]
[03:00] Evan: ok, hitting the endpoint here, note the model is redwood/3-large-quantized (demo config), using prefix caching so repeated patient context is quick.
[03:18] Tom: pause — can you explain quantized tradeoffs? customers ask about quality hit.
[03:24] Evan: sure, quantization reduces memory and improves throughput; our Optimize tool suggests profiles per workload — if you need strict fidelity we recommend fp16 on Dedicated for critical ops. small transcription glitch: "qualtiy" in audio.
[03:45] Priya: good. now hit a simulated spike to show fallback policy.
[03:50] [Evan throttles local script to simulate spike]
[04:05] Evan: trigger fallback — system reroutes to compatible variant in another region with slightly higher latency but kept under SLA.
[04:22] Tom: what about cost impact when you fallback?
[04:25] Hannah: call out tradeoffs — fallback can increase unit-cost by 10-40% depending on model variant; flip to cost-savings levers: batching, caching, quantization, and routing by cost tier.
[04:40] Tom: procurement will ask for numbers. do we have a slide or a spreadsheet?
[04:45] Priya: yes — link to benchmark spreadsheet shared: https://redwood.local/benchmarks/roleplay-may2025 (internal). Evan, remind folks to snapshot the latency/cost table.
[04:58] Evan: noted.
[05:05] Tom: competitor angle — Anthropic claims safer outputs; how do we handle safety/regression?
[05:12] Priya: say: "we provide continuous evals tied to your prompt tests, rollback and canary deploys, and quality-monitoring alerts". avoid making claims about model design; focus on operational controls.
[05:30] Sana: legal will ask about data access by model providers — do we ever share customer data with third parties?
[05:36] Hannah: no by default; for hosted theres a clear policy, and for Dedicated/Private you control keys and retention. recommend sending security pack. link to deck: https://redwood.local/security/enterprise-pack.pdf
[05:55] Priya: ok pivot — role reversal: Evan act as the buyer pressing on an outage scenario. show incident response.
[06:05] Evan (roleplay buyer): we saw a 15-minute outage last month on another vendor, what happens if Redwood has a zone failure?
[06:12] Priya: describe multi-region routing, automatic fallback, and how console shows per-route live metrics. be explicit about RTO/RPO and communication plan.
[06:28] Tom: great, now critique the language — it sounded too technical for procurement.
[06:33] Priya: good feedback — have two scripts: technical for SEs and business for AEs. business script: "we provide predictable SLAs, a clear escalation path, and a dedicated technical contact for onboarding and runbooks".
[06:50] [Feedback round — 15 min]
[07:05] Marta: note on messaging: avoid saying "we re-invented the runtime" — that triggers skepticism. use "high-throughput serving runtime" instead.
[07:20] Evan: objection practice — Tom plays finance, ask hard on unit economics.
[07:30] Tom (roleplay finance): your price per 1M tokens is higher than AWS baseline; make the case for total cost of ownership.
[07:40] Hannah: counter with example: "when you include latency penalties, re-requests, and engineering ops to tune on-prem, Redwood reduces your real per-conversation cost by X%" — use customer case studies. small stutter in audio: "percent-age".
[07:58] Priya: callout: give a short two-sentence ROI: "we lower per-conversation compute cost via caching/batching and reduce ops overhead with a unified control plane". rehearse that.
[08:12] Tom: demo hiccup — you simulated a hallucination earlier; how do you present safety mitigations?
[08:18] Evan: show the function-calling layer that turns unsafe spans into structured outputs and has a reject path. mention dataflow filters and human-in-loop escalation.
[08:35] [Timestamped note: transcription occasionally swaps "function calling" to "function calling" - noisy mic]
[08:45] Priya: tactical tip — always ask what metrics they care about: p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, and error rate. keep those front and center.
[09:00] Tom: roleplay end, now live critique from the SEs.
[09:05] Hannah: plus two from me — 1) shorten the demo to a 3-min hook then jump into FAQ; 2) prepare a short procurement slide that maps policy questions to exact artifacts and owners.
[09:20] Evan: add a 30-second "what if" script about private deployment timeline and sample checklist for security approval.
[09:35] Priya: noted. Marta: capture next steps and owners.
[09:42] [Longer segment — planning the follow-up roleplay focused on procurement/legal, ~10 min discussion]
[20:00] Priya: ok last practice — rapid-fire objections. Marta play procurement.
[20:08] Marta (roleplay procurement): "We need right to audit and a BAA — can you sign?"
[20:14] Priya: say "we have a standard BAA for PHI use; for Private deployments we can support self-hosted audit logs and customer-managed encryption".
[20:28] Marta: good but avoid committing to custom engineering. phrase as: "we can support via our Private deployment offering and will engage solutions engineering for scoping".
[20:40] Tom: after objection practice, cadence for follow-ups?
[20:45] Priya: propose: AE sends updated script + slides within 48 hrs, SE sends short demo clip and benchmark snapshot within 4 business days, schedule procurement roleplay next week.
[21:00] [Recap and close — 4 min]
[21:05] Priya: quick recap — three deliverables, owners: Priya (script + slides), Evan (demo clip), Hannah (bench slides). we will post notes in #field-playbooks.
[21:20] Evan: one more note: in demos, avoid model brand names beyond saying "open models and verified profiles" — keeps attention on operational benefits.
[21:35] Tom: thanks team — felt realistic, please send the one-pager for procurement.
[21:40] Priya: will do. closing.
[21:45] [Meeting ends; approximate total 78 minutes; longer segments collapsed in transcript above for brevity]
